result: {"score":3,"reasons":"The answer matches the reference on every rubric point. Order is snooze, then dedup, then canary and create_case checks, then case creation. In filter_snooze, an expired filter hits `break` and stops the loop. An empty expression snoozes everything. The 45-minute default comes from SIGNAL_DEFAULT_DEDUP_WINDOW_MINUTES and applies only when the signal has no filters at all. It calls the docstring's \"1 hour\" stale. Per-filter windows are in seconds, and it gives the 3600 column default and the 600 Pydantic default. Dedup requires a shared entity and picks the earliest match. Canary instances are never deduplicated, can be snoozed, and never open a case. The extra claims, such as a possible null case_id in the filter branch, don't contradict the reference. It doesn't mention that the UI labels windows as minutes, but that is a minor gap."}

structured_output.reasons: The answer matches the reference on every rubric point. Order is snooze, then dedup, then canary and create_case checks, then case creation. In filter_snooze, an expired filter hits `break` and stops the loop. An empty expression snoozes everything. The 45-minute default comes from SIGNAL_DEFAULT_DEDUP_WINDOW_MINUTES and applies only when the signal has no filters at all. It calls the docstring's "1 hour" stale. Per-filter windows are in seconds, and it gives the 3600 column default and the 600 Pydantic default. Dedup requires a shared entity and picks the earliest match. Canary instances are never deduplicated, can be snoozed, and never open a case. The extra claims, such as a possible null case_id in the filter branch, don't contradict the reference. It doesn't mention that the UI labels windows as minutes, but that is a minor gap.
